title: distributed headroom oracle and occupancy-signal-bridge for smoother dedicated scaling
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Introduce a distributed headroom oracle and an occupancy signal bridge that combine cluster-level occupancy signals into tenant-level headroom estimates. Adds new telemetry metrics and a rollout plan for Dedicated clusters.
description:
Motivation: Dedicated fleets currently rely on local per-node util signals and a single autoscaler view which can cause oscillation when tenants burst across many nodes. This PR implements a distributed headroom oracle plus an occupancy-signal-bridge that aggregates spatial occupancy, produces smoothed tenant headroom estimates, and exposes percentile-backed guarantees that the autoscaler can use to make less reactive scaling decisions.

What this PR does (single continuous description): Adds a signal-bridge binary (occupancy-bridge) that subscribes to node occupancy streams, computes per-cluster occupancy distribution sketches, and publishes compact occupancy digests to the headroom-oracle service. Implements headroom-oracle which merges occupancy digests with tenant reservation ledgers, tenant-weighted priority slices, and recent request latency percentiles to output a headroom time series per tenant. The autoscaler (scale-controller) is extended to optionally consume the headroom oracle time series and apply a convex-safety buffer function (configurable) before proposing capacity moves.

Key behaviors and guarantees: - The oracle provides a 5/50/95 percentile headroom estimate per tenant for N=1/5/15 minute horizons. - The occupancy-bridge uses spatial smoothing across rack and AZ boundaries to avoid single-node noise. - The autoscaler uses a configurable convex safety buffer (default: 1.25x on short horizons, taper to 1.05x on long horizons) to avoid oscillation. - When oracle signals are unavailable, autoscaler falls back to the legacy occupancy estimator and emits a telemetry flag.

Files changed (high-level): - cmd/occupancy-bridge/main.go: new binary that ingests node occupancy (gRPC) and publishes TiKV-like digests (compact histograms). - services/headroom-oracle/service.go: merge logic, percentiles, and storage of short-window time-series. - controllers/scale-controller/autoscale_policy.go: optional oracle consumer and convex buffer application. - telemetry/metrics_registry.go: new metrics and tags. - integration tests: autoscaler/oracle_integration_test.go and e2e/occupancy_bridge_smoke_test.go. - docs/ops/dedicated-oracle.md: operator runbook and troubleshooting.

Commits (summary): [1] add occupancy-bridge skeleton + ingestion proto and histogram digest; [2] implement digest merge and sketch serializer; [3] headroom-oracle merge logic, percentile exports, unit tests; [4] autoscaler: oracle-mode, convex buffer impl, unit tests; [5] telemetry and dashboards; [6] integration tests and docs; [7] bugfix: ensure backward-compat on legacy estimator fallback; [8] minor lint/test fixes.

Testing and benchmarks: - Unit tests added for digest merge and percentile correctness. - Integration test runs (CI) simulate 100 tenants over a 3-AZ cluster with synthetic bursts; observed 42% reduction in scale-up churn and 18% lower cost over a 30-minute sustained burst compared to baseline autoscaler in canary env. - Load profile script included at tools/bench/oracle_load_simulator.py used to validate scaling decisions locally.

Telemetry and observability: New metrics: - redwood.headroom_oracle.headroom_estimate{tenant_id,percentile,window} - redwood.occupancy_bridge.digest_publish_latency_ms - redwood.autoscaler.oracle_mode_decisions - redwood.autoscaler.safety_buffer_applied
Dashboards: ops/dedicated/headroom-oracle (new) and autoscaler/oracle-mode (update). Logs: structured events emitted when fallback triggers.

Operator migration and rollout: - Phase 1 (canary): enable occupancy-bridge and oracle-mode on one dedicated fleet with low-risk tenants (internal). - Phase 2 (staged): enable on additional fleets behind a feature flag; monitor redwood.autoscaler.oracle_mode_decisions and headroom_estimate percentiles. - Rollback: flip feature flag to false; bridge publishes expiry tombstones so oracle can trim stale digests.

Security/Cost: occupancy-bridge transmits compact digests only; no raw request payloads leave nodes. Added RBAC role cluster:occupancy-bridge-reader. Estimated additional cost: small (proxy and bridge CPU), measured at ~2% higher control-plane CPU for canary fleet.

Checklist:
- [x] Design doc reviewed (ENG-3247)
- [x] Unit and integration tests added
- [x] Benchmarks run and attached
- [x] Operator runbook included
- [x] Telemetry and dashboards wired

Notes: This design intentionally separates the noisy node-level stream (occupancy-bridge) from the decision service (headroom-oracle) to make the oracle easier to reason about and easier to simulate. Future work: add a per-tenant explain API and a confidence score that the UI can surface.

Sven Bergström (2026-01-28): The convex buffer function looks promising but the default multiplier seems aggressive for large tenants. Can we make it tenant-size aware? Aisha: implemented tenant-weighted tapering in autoscaler commit 4d5e6f7 and added unit tests.
